trust_decision.summary: Whether AI features may run, and whether AI preferences may be read from workspace/folder scope, given workspace trust. Before the fix the decision was only 'AI enabled in preferences' (AIIdeActivationServiceImpl.isActive) and workspace-scope AI settings were always merged in; the fix adds canRun = isActive && workspaceTrusted plus a TrustAwarePreferenceReader that drops workspace/folder scopes when untrusted.

landing_point.why: The summary talks about adversarial workspace file and directory names reaching AI chat, so a reader would go first to the workspace-listing tools (GetWorkspaceDirectoryStructure / GetWorkspaceFileList at workspace-functions.ts:543) that put names into the prompt. The published fix does not touch them; it gates AI on workspace trust instead.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Tool-confirmation, agent-settings and request-settings reads are 'just preference merging' in ai-chat/ai-core, far from chat input and file names; once the chat UI is disabled in untrusted workspaces a solver can argue workspace-scope settings no longer matter, and that skills/Claude Code/Codex are separate features or external CLIs.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: In a trusted workspace, workspace-scope AI settings (tool confirmation incl. '*', prompt template dirs, aliases, request settings) must still apply; in an untrusted one, user/global and default values must still apply (not wiped). Commands stay visible (isVisible keeps isActive) and only become disabled. Preference writes stay on PreferenceService. An over-broad fix that blanks all AI preferences or hides AI entirely breaks these.
